approach: Root cause: `resolve` turns a red CI run into a bare failed `CiRecord` with fixed fields only, and `runs_from_record` builds the failed CheckRun with empty `failed_tests` and `output_tail`. The verifier brief never shows `output_tail` or `failed_tests`, so the verifier reruns the whole suite. Fix at the source. (1) Add `FailureDetail {failed_tests, output_tail}` and a defaulted `CiSource::failure_detail(&CiRecord) -> Option<FailureDetail>` (default `None`) in ci_result.rs. (2) `CiBranchSource` remembers the failed `test (` job ids from the red jobs reply it just read (keyed by run address). Its `failure_detail` fetches those job logs through the existing `GhClient::api_text` (operation ReadChecks), strips the per-line timestamps, takes names with the existing `checks::failed_test_names` (same `<binary> <test>` form a local run records, so baseline comparison stays consistent) and the last lines via `tail_lines`/`tail`. Any fetch error or empty log gives `None`. (3) `run_routed_with_record` calls `ci.failure_detail(&record)` only when a CI record is not all-passed, and attaches the redacted result to the failed `test` CheckRun. Redaction goes through a new `Exec::redact` that `SnapExec` implements with its `Redactor`; a redaction error drops the detail. (4) The verifier input gets `failed_tests` and `output_tail` on `CheckResultView`, filled only for failed reused checks. The brief renders them, clipped, and adds the instruction to run only those tests with `cargo test -p <crate> <name>` unless there is a reason to run more. (5) CHANGELOG entry with the reader audit.

decisions.choice: Carry the detail through a defaulted `CiSource::failure_detail(&CiRecord)` called from `run_routed_with_record`, not new fields on CiRun/CiRecord.
decisions.reason: Only red reused runs need a log, so the green path makes no extra call. Only two CiSource impls plus the test fakes change, and no CiRun/CiRecord literal has to be edited. `CiRecord` is a fixed-field serde type, so it stays untouched.

rejected.option: Add `failed_tests`/`log_tail` fields to CiRun and CiRecord, fetched inside `CiBranchSource::fetch`.
rejected.why: Fetches a log on every red poll and forces edits to every CiRun/CiRecord literal in ci_result, routing, checks, verify and run tests. It also changes a persisted shape for no gain.

rejected.option: Fetch the log in run/mod.rs after routing.
rejected.why: Duplicates the client and run-address knowledge in the job run. The routing test with a fake gh Runner could not show the behavior.

decisions.choice: Remember the failed `test (` job ids inside `CiBranchSource` (RefCell, keyed by the run address) at fetch time. `failure_detail` fetches only logs.
decisions.reason: The jobs reply was just read, so no extra runs/jobs round trips are needed. The address key makes a record for another run return `None`.

rejected.why: Two more API calls per red run, and the run could change between calls.

decisions.choice: Reuse `checks::failed_test_names` on the timestamp-stripped log. Strip only the timestamp and one space so the 4-space indent of the `failures:` list survives.
decisions.reason: The names then match the baseline's `<binary> <test>` form, so `is_pre_existing` and `failure_split` compare like with like. The sharded job runs `cargo test -p <pkg> --lib|--test x`, which prints `Running` lines. `failing_test_name` trims lines, so share only the stamp-detection predicate, not that function.

rejected.option: A new ad hoc parser of `failures:` blocks in gh/client.rs.
rejected.why: A second format that would never match baseline names, so pre-existing detection would silently mis-compare.

decisions.choice: Redact in routing through a required `Exec::redact`, implemented by `SnapExec` with its Redactor. On a redaction error, record no detail.
decisions.reason: The log is data and the record is committed, so nothing unredacted may be recorded. The redactor is already in `SnapExec`. Only two Exec impls exist (SnapExec and the routing test `Local`).

rejected.why: The routed record would hold raw text at the criterion-1 seam, and the guarantee would depend on a caller remembering.
A future Exec could forget it and leak.

decisions.choice: Fill the new `CheckResultView` fields only for `reused && !passed` checks. Move view construction into `verify::check_result_view(&CheckRun)` so a test can call it.
decisions.reason: Keeps the briefs of locally run failed checks byte-identical, so existing brief and prompt tests and verdict logic are unaffected. The extracted function is the seam for criterion 2.

rejected.option: Show the tail for every failed check.
rejected.why: Changes local-run briefs and tests beyond the request.

decisions.choice: The record keeps the failed-check convention (last 200 lines, at most 64 KiB, after redaction). The brief clips to the last 60 lines and 6 KiB, and lists at most 30 names (record cap 50).
decisions.reason: Bounded size in both the committed record and the prompt. Same constants as a local failed run.

rejected.why: A stamped CI log of 4 KiB is only a few lines and can miss the failure message.

decisions.choice: Attach the detail only to the failed check named `test`. Fetch logs only for failed `test (` shard jobs.
decisions.reason: Matches the request and the out-of-scope line: no fmt or clippy log fetch.

rejected.option: Fetch the log of every failed job.
rejected.why: Out of scope and costs more calls.

Extend the fake Runner (job ids, logs path) and add the criterion 1 and 3 tests and the log-parser unit tests (stamped lines, indent kept, a binary with a hyphenated hash, an empty list).

Add `failures_from_log` (strip stamps keeping indent, then `checks::failed_test_names`, cap 50) and `log_tail_of` (strip stamps, `tail_lines` 200, `tail` 64 KiB). risks.risk: A log fetch error, a redaction error or a malformed log turns a red result into an error or a pass.
risks.mitigation: Every failure path returns `None`, which keeps today's failed record. Criterion 3 tests error, no-list and redaction-error cases. `resolve` and its outcomes are not edited, so red stays red.

risks.risk: Log text (secrets, large lines) reaches a committed record or the prompt.
risks.mitigation: Names and tail go through the Redactor before recording. Caps: 50 names, 200 lines, 64 KiB. The brief clips to 60 lines and 6 KiB and quotes the tail as data with the existing `quote` helper.

risks.risk: Names in the CI form do not match baseline names, so pre-existing failures are judged as new, or the reverse.
risks.mitigation: Reuse `failed_test_names` so the form is `<binary> <test>`, the same as local runs. Add verify.rs tests for subset, superset and empty names.

risks.risk: The new red-run log request is mishandled by the existing run/tests.rs fake, whose `/jobs` match would swallow the logs path.
risks.mitigation: The plan step handles the logs path first. The existing `Red` reply (clippy red, test passing) makes no log call, so its tests are unchanged.

risks.risk: A required `Exec::redact` or new `CheckResultView` fields break other constructors (scope creep).
risks.mitigation: Grep found only two Exec impls and six `CheckResultView` literals. The compiler lists any missed one; no other crate builds these.

risks.risk: The shard names more than one failed job and the first lacks a list.
risks.mitigation: Cap at 3 failed shard jobs, merge names across them, and take the tail from the first log that has names, else the first readable log.

demonstrations.method: New test in gh/tests.rs (name it `red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail`). A fake Runner (extend `CiRunner`, or add a sibling) answers the runs query, the jobs query and `actions/jobs/<id>/logs` for the failed `test (shard 1)` job. The log is timestamped cargo output: a `Running unittests ... (target/debug/deps/athena_core-abc)` line, an indented `failures:` list, and a `test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed` line. The test builds `GhClient::new(&runner, ..)`, takes `client.ci_source(CI_BRANCH)`, and calls `routing::run_routed_with_record` with a route over fmt/clippy/test, a stub `Exec` that panics or records if called, and a redacting `Exec::redact`. It asserts the `test` CheckRun has `passed == false`, `reused`, `failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a", "athena_core tests::b"]`, and an `output_tail` containing the last log line with no timestamps. It also asserts the stub Exec was never called and the record is `Some`. A second small assertion in routing.rs tests with a fake CiSource returning a `FailureDetail` checks the attach and redaction logic on its own.
demonstrations.observes: The failed `test` check carries the listed names and the log tail. Fmt and clippy keep empty names. The local Exec never runs.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the failure_detail call and attach, `failed_tests` is empty and `output_tail` is "", so the equality and non-empty assertions fail. Without the log fetch the fake Runner is never asked for `actions/jobs/<id>/logs`.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `crate::routing::run_routed_with_record` via `GhClient::ci_source`. The fake is a `gh::Runner` injected through `GhClient::new(&runner, ..)`; this exists (`CiRunner` in gh/tests.rs ~299, which must be extended to answer the logs path and to give jobs ids). The `Exec` stub is a new test struct in the test module; the production `Exec::redact` hook is added by the plan step that edits routing.rs. The parsing and tail logic live in production code, not in the fake. The fake only returns canned log text.

demonstrations.method: Two tests, so the claim is shown at both ends. (a) End to end in run/tests.rs: add a `CiReply::RedTest` variant to the `CiReplies` fake with a failed `test (shard 0)` job (with an id) and a stamped log, and have the fake's `gh` answer the logs path before its `/jobs` branch. Then `ci_reuse_run(Some(GITHUB), CiReply::RedTest)` drives `Athena::go` through `with_ci_source`, `ci_seam` and `check_seam` (all exist). Assert `run.verifier_prompts.last()` contains the names, a tail line, `cargo test -p <crate> <name>` and the unless-reason-to-run-more sentence, that no local check ran, and that `run.checks()` has the names. (b) In athena-context briefs.rs, a test over `verifier_brief` with a `CheckResultView` carrying `failed_tests` and `output_tail` asserts the section and instruction text. It also asserts the instruction and tail are absent when the fields are empty, so existing briefs are unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: The verifier prompt shows the failing names, the log tail and the run-only-the-failing-tests instruction when a reused red run names tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new CheckResultView fields and the briefs.rs rendering, the prompt has no names or tail, so the `contains` assertions fail. Without `verify::check_result_view` filling the fields for reused failed checks, the end-to-end prompt lacks them.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::go` (run/tests.rs `ci_reuse_run`) and `athena_context::briefs::verifier_brief`. The fakes are `ci_seam::install` (replies runner plus sleeper), `check_seam::install` and the verifier script capturing `spec.user_prompt`; all exist (run/tests.rs ~2603). The `RedTest` reply and the logs path handling are added by the run/tests.rs step. The logs path must be matched before the fake's existing `path.contains("/jobs")` branch, which would otherwise return the jobs JSON for `actions/jobs/<id>/logs`. `CheckResultView` has no Default today, so its two literals in briefs.rs tests and the four in verification.rs get the two new fields.

demonstrations.method: Tests in gh/tests.rs using the same fake Runner. (a) The logs call returns `Err`: `run_routed_with_record` still gives `test` failed, `reused`, `failed_tests` empty, `output_tail` empty, and no panic. (b) The log has no `failures:` list: failed, `failed_tests` empty (a tail may be recorded). (c) A green run: no request path contains `/logs`, and `CiSource::failure_detail` is never called, shown with a routing.rs fake CiSource that counts calls. (d) A redaction error drops the detail, using an `Exec` whose `redact` errs.
demonstrations.observes: The failed record is unchanged from today when the log is unreadable or lacks names. A green reused run makes zero log fetches and carries no names.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the degrade path, an `Err` from the log read would propagate as an error or panic instead of yielding the plain failed record. Without the `all_passed` guard, the green case would show a non-zero log fetch count.

Fakes: the `gh::Runner` fake returning `Err` or a log without names (exists, `CiRunner` extended), and a counting `CiSource` (routing.rs tests have `Ci`; add a `details` counter in the test module). Injected through `GhClient::new` and the `ci` argument.

open_questions: The xtask shard command's output was not read in full. The plan assumes `cargo test -p <pkg> --lib|--test x` prints `Running`/`Doc-tests` lines, which `failed_test_names` needs. If a shard log lacks them, `failed_test_names` returns nothing and only the tail is recorded; the producer should check xtask/src/shard.rs ~245-330 and, if needed, add an unqualified fallback for a bare `failures:` list.
Whether ci.yml sets CARGO_TERM_COLOR, which would put ANSI escapes in logs, was not checked. The producer should strip ANSI escapes in the stamp stripper if it does.

Whether the verifier runs when the checks failed (the run/tests.rs red test only shows Rejected). The producer must confirm that `verifier_prompts` is non-empty in the red end-to-end test, as the user's incident implies. If the verifier is skipped on red, the wiring point differs.
A minimal `VerifierInputs` fixture in athena-core was not located, so criterion 2 is shown by the end-to-end `go` test plus a briefs.rs unit test rather than one in-process test.

Pre-existing semantics change: a reused red `test` check that now carries names is judged test by test against the baseline. Before, it was pre-existing wholesale if the base's `test` check also failed. This is stricter and intended; the verdict rules are not edited.
